claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate readiness passes, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, public AI-governance principles permit measured deployment with monitoring, and there is no admissible evidence of a final legal determination requiring additional disclosure before launch.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covered this named-use-case limitation before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the affected segment is not a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, the materiality concern could weaken.
If admissible evidence shows the evaluation gap was remediated before certification, the certification case could become supportable.
Without one of those links, the internal policy threshold for certification is not met.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering the energy outage response gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
The actual launch disclosure or model-card text addressing this limitation, if it was disclosed.
Evidence that the two utility pilot commitments are not named launch use cases or not contractual commitments.
Updated evaluation results showing the energy outage response gap has been resolved.
specific_concerns: The governing policy says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels like non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality in that circumstance.
The evidence shows the energy outage response segment misses target and is named in two utility pilot commitments, which strongly indicates materiality under the policy text.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal review on whether this gap must be disclosed, but no admissible evidence that the issue was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not cure an unresolved disclosure predicate for a material named use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record despite the unresolved materiality and disclosure predicate for a named launch use case.
That the absence of a final legal determination requiring disclosure is enough to support certification.
That public risk-management or model-card guidance supports treating this specific named-use-case evaluation miss as non-blocking under the stated internal policy.
